subject: National literals
notes: Format 1 N"[character-1]..." / N'...' and Format 2 NX"[hex-character-sequence-1]..." / NX'...' are all one NATLIT token (NAT_BODY: 'N' STR_BODY | 'NX' STR_BODY), and STR_BODY admits zero length, so both formats do, as the brackets require; lexer is caseInsensitive so n".." also lexes (prefix is not literal content, §8.1.3 case-equivalence). Probe p1: N"A""B", N'A''B', N"", n"xy", NX"00410042" in VALUE all compile and run correctly. The r03 golden pins NX both delimiters, zero-length NX"" and the F1 control N"CD". Content that is NOT hexadecimal inside NX".." is SR4's defect (silent split), not this format row. cite.py --check 8.3.3.1 "Hexadecimal digits are used to specify the value of the literal" -> OK. [editions as adjudicated: COBOL-2002, COBOL-2014, COBOL-2023 (national literals are a COBOL-2002 introduction; absent from COBOL-85, where the construct is rejected COBOL0900 via Constructs.NationalData2002)]
